name: StepPlayerState2
evidence: StepPlayer's branch for mode 2: turns the collider toward its rotation target, then by the sub-state steers its position toward a point offset by the stick's polar offset or by animation marker times

name: ControlPlayerState2
evidence: ControlPlayer's mode 2 control (called with the pad): by the sub-state turns the pad stick into a polar aim offset and heading, handles the jump, grab and step requests and changes the sub-state

name: ComputeLedgeEdgeOffset
evidence: for a mesh edge whose two faces are one flat (normal z above 0.7) and one steep (below 0.55), computes the offset from the player to the flat face's edge; returns 0 for other edges

name: TestProbeSegmentsAgainstColliders
evidence: for each of the 11 segment pairs of D_00263EC0 transformed by the matrix, tests every unflagged part of the world's collider list with func_00141C28 and returns whether at least two hits had a normal above 0.7

name: ComputeLedgeOffsetForContact
evidence: by the contact kind (1 vertex, 2 and 3 edge or face), sums ComputeLedgeEdgeOffset over the mesh edges around the contact's key and writes the offset; returns 1 when any edge counted

name: FindPlayerLedgeContact
evidence: unless a grab just ended (0.15 s), walks the player's contacts for ledge-capable parts, picks the lowest valid contact whose ledge offset exists and whose probe point is not inside the tree, and returns it with its side and position

name: ChoosePlayerNextState
evidence: returns the state the callers hand to SetPlayerState with sub-state -1 (ControlPlayer, func_0017F018): 0 unless the speed at +0x634 is above 0, then 1 when +0x900 is set, 5 when +0xA10 is, else 0

name: CollectPlayerHoldQueries
evidence: flags the colliders in a sphere around the player and queues a kind-0x20 query (FindNodeForQuery) for each class 0x75 object and each collider or mesh hit within range and the vertical band around the player's anchor

name: ShouldPlayerLaunchAtTarget
evidence: original assembly: uses back-memory scratch and SolveActiveSetSystem to decide whether the player's current target can be reached; the player's state 0 update calls it and then LaunchPlayerAtTarget when it returns non-zero

name: UpdatePlayerState2
evidence: UpdatePlayer's mode 2 update: by the sub-state places the player on the target point or curve, tracks the leap's landing height, restarts after timeouts with ChoosePlayerNextState and seeks the animation marker

name: SolveArrivalTimeAtHeight
evidence: solves the quadratic of half the gravity (+0x358) with the z differences of its four points (SolveQuadratic) and writes the later positive root; returns 0 when there is none (StartNextQueueEntry, func_001CE590)

name: ComputePlayerJumpVelocity
evidence: copies the player's velocity (+0x150) and sets its z by the jump kind at +0x224C (jtbl_0024B150): a square root of the height at +0x700 times one of D_00263E80/88/8C, or twice the drop from +0x148 to +0x6A8 plus D_00263E84 times +0x358, never below the current z; SetPlayerState and StartNextQueueEntry call it

name: ComputeUpwardBoostVelocity
evidence: copies the object's velocity and replaces its z with a clamped quadratic of z, never below the current z; used by the player's states 10 and 11 and the target launch

name: ComputeUpwardBoostVelocityUnitSlope
evidence: as ComputeUpwardBoostVelocity with the second pair of curve constants (D_00264070 = 682 + 1.0 z, D_00264080 caps it at 682) where the first has slope 0.5; the player's state 3 and the entry queue's case 2 call it
